newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya policeman charged in Irishman's murder.
newsitem.headline: Kenya policeman charged in Irishman's murder.

text.p: A Kenyan policeman has been charged with murdering an Irish Roman Catholic missionary at a school in central Kenya, Nairobi newspapers said on Tuesday.

They said 35-year-old Francis Kimanzi Mbaya was not required to plead when he appeared at a court in the town of Nakuru northwest of Nairobi on Monday charged with the murder of Brother Larry Timmons at a school in nearby Lare on January 21.
The Daily Nation newspaper said earlier on Monday priests, nuns and monks from parishes in the Nakuru region met the local provincial commissioner and complained about insecurity.
Provincial Commissioner Yusuf Haji said the government was shocked by the shooting of Timmons by a policeman who should maintain law and order and protect members of the public.
He said police should differentiate between attackers and victims and promised to bring to justice anyone implicated in the murder.
Kimanzi was remanded in custody until February 10. The East African Standard daily said Timmons was killed when police responded to residents saying robbers were raiding Lare school.
The Nakuru Roman Catholic diocese on Saturday demanded an explanation for the shooting of the 40-year-old missionary and three other violent robberies at Catholic missions this month.
It said in a statement that Timmons was shot by a policeman one day after he confronted local officials over bribery and discrimination surrounding the issuing of new identity cards.
"We cannot help but relate the killing with the prior confrontation between our brother and the administration," it said.
The London-based human rights group Amnesty International said this month Kenya's government had failed to halt the widespread torture of men, women and children. The government denied the report.
